question.text: The energy spectrum of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">β</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math>[number <math> <mrow> <mi>N</mi><mfenced> <mi>E</mi> </mfenced></mrow> </math> as a function of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">β</mi><mo>-</mo></math>energy <math><mi>E</mi></math>] emitted from a radioactive source is

solution.text:
In β - decay, energy emission is continuous and energy is shared between β - particles and daughter nuclei.
Thus certain β -particles have zero energy and certain have maximum energy.
Option (1) is most appropriate
